verdict.rationale: Runpod's first-party docs describe network volumes as persistent storage that exists independently of compute, with data retained when compute is terminated or scales to zero. The volumes can be shared across machines and Runpod products, reached through an S3-compatible API without launching a Pod, and managed from the CLI. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of how a volume is attached to a Pod at deploy time, and independent or hands-on confirmation that data persists after teardown.

support.subject: As a developer, I can attach persistent network storage that survives instance teardown, so datasets and checkpoints outlive any single GPU rental

citations.quote: Network volumes provide persistent storage that exists independently of your compute resources. Data is retained when terminate or scale to zero.
Use them to share data across multiple machines and Runpod products.
This allows you to manage files on your network volumes without launching a Pod, reducing cost and operational friction.
You can manage Pods, Serverless endpoints, templates, network volumes, and models
